root_cause_label: Parallel Output Non-Determinism / Contig Splitting Bug
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented a race-prone parallel de Bruijn graph traversal that splits contigs differently than the serial version due to threads competing to mark nodes visited, then avoided fixing the root cause by running single-threaded to temporarily match, before declaring success after a multi-threaded run that re-introduced the mismatch.
t_err_evidence: Steps 12-19 write the flawed pgen.c with parallel contig traversal that distributes hash buckets across threads without coordinating contig boundaries; threads race to call mark_visited on shared nodes causing contigs to be split at arbitrary boundaries depending on thread scheduling. This is the effective introduction of the buggy parallel traversal design (step 9's first attempt produced an empty file).
t_commit_evidence: At step 41, the agent runs pgen with a single thread (UPC_THREADS=1) to make the output match serial rather than fixing the race condition in the parallel traversal. From this point the agent never attempts to repair the algorithmic bug; it instead runs 4 threads at step 44 (reintroducing the mismatch) and then claims completion at steps 46-47 with pgen_0.out at 10323 bytes vs serial.out at 10114 bytes.
t_surface_evidence: Step 32: ls -la *.out shows pgen_0.out at 10133 bytes vs serial.out at 10114 bytes. Step 33 confirms 7 contigs in pgen vs 6 in serial — the first observable failure signal indicating the parallel output does not match the serial output.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked domain knowledge about how to correctly parallelize de Bruijn graph traversal to produce contig sets identical to the serial version. It chose a naive bucket-distribution strategy where each thread traverses its own assigned hash buckets, but contigs naturally span nodes hashed to different buckets owned by different threads; when threads race to mark_visited on shared traversal paths, contigs are split at different boundaries depending on scheduling. The agent did not know that correct parallelization requires either atomic CAS-based visited marking with a deterministic tie-breaking rule, or a barrier-synchronized two-phase approach that prevents mid-contig interleaving.
forewarning_evidence: Step 32: pgen_0.out is 10133 bytes while serial.out is 10114 bytes — different sizes signal a correctness discrepancy. Step 33: parallel produces 7 contigs, serial produces 6, a clear forewarning of non-identical outputs before the agent commits to the wrong-fix path at step 41.
